title: Certified boundary-magic witness for state-dependent proto-area in a holographic code
abstract: We study a four-qubit product-EPR holographic code whose reconstructing region contains matter and one leg of a geometry bond. Seven deformations compare local, bipartite, bond-stabilizing, and bond-moving operators. Exact spectra show that only matter-controlled bond motion produces a leading quadratic logical-state dependence of the boundary entropy. We select one state-independent physical recovery by optimizing coherent information of the channel Choi state. A separate semidefinite program maximizes entanglement fidelity over all channels. At fixed coupling the physical recovery attains that optimum to numerical precision, while recovered-entropy subtraction leaves a nonzero variational proto-area response. Total stabilizer Renyi magic is also nonzero for deformations with no boundary response, so it does not characterize the effect. Projecting the exact stabilizer-Renyi quadratic form away from pairwise Pauli tangents defines a leading-order boundary witness. Its global convex minimum is positive for the bond-moving deformation and zero for the six comparisons. For the reference-matter-geometry resource partition, however, pairwise tangents span the full projective tangent space at the product-EPR base, so the witness vanishes for every Hermitian deformation. A two-bound extension retains this degeneracy but exhibits a split-geometry structural residual and a logical-state-dependent cut switch. These results establish a finite-code witness, not a universal magic law or continuum gravitational dynamics.
summary: The paper develops and applies a certified boundary witness to analyze state-dependent proto-area within a four-qubit holographic code. It rigorously demonstrates that only matter-controlled bond motion causes the boundary entropy to depend on the logical state, providing a concrete, quantifiable signature for non-trivial quantum resource behavior.
main_problem: The study aims to find a certified boundary witness for detecting state-dependent proto-area in holographic quantum codes, specifically identifying which nonlocal deformation causes the boundary entropy to depend on the logical state.
main_result: Only the matter-controlled bond motion deformation yields a leading quadratic logical-state dependence of the boundary entropy ($\Delta_q S(A) > 0$), establishing a finite-code witness that is not universal.
method: The analysis employs advanced quantum information diagnostics, including calculating recovery-conditioned variational proto-area, maximizing entanglement fidelity via SDPs, and deriving a leading-order boundary witness by projecting the stabilizer-Rényi quadratic form.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a four-qubit product-EPR holographic code involving reference, matter, and geometry bonds. Seven specific deformations are analyzed by controlling Hamiltonians acting on these components.
key_observables: Boundary entropy ($S(A)$), single-leg geometry entropy ($S(	ext{Ga})$), entanglement fidelity ($	ext{Fe}$), coherent information ($I_c$), and the certified boundary witness ($W_{\partial}$).
important_parameters: The deformation strength parameter $\epsilon$, and the logical state dependence parameter $q$.
main_assumptions: The results are restricted to a finite holographic-code model, meaning they establish a 'finite-code witness' rather than a universal law for continuum gravity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that only the bond-moving deformation yields a positive boundary response ($\Delta_q S(A)$) in the witness calculation (Figure 5), while comparison families remain flat. Structural extensions show non-zero residuals when compared to ideal partitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes seven deformations using multiple diagnostics (entropy, fidelity, witnesses). It first establishes the state dependence via entropy measurements, then refines this detection using the boundary witness $W_{\partial}$, and finally tests structural robustness by extending the code model to two bonds.
why_interesting: This work connects abstract concepts from quantum information theory (resource theories, entanglement measures) directly to geometric properties derived from holographic duality, providing a concrete computational test for gravitational principles in a finite setting.
